column1: # ══ ROUND 2 ══ the six PICK-RESOLVE rows from the Gate-1 force-pick set, plus the two spectro/
# rows re-routed to PICK-RESOLVE (see known-commits.tsv D-1 audit). Judged on: what fork behavior
# can be LOST when a 3-way merge lands this on v1.16.1, weighted by whether a wrong resolution
# fails LOUDLY (build/CI error, caught at Tier-1) or SILENTLY (compiles, deploys, wrong at runtime).
# Each is backed by reading the fork diff against the actual v1.16.1 tree.
# 9767d35a "Controller and Webhook separation" — palette's deployment model IS this commit, and
# both failure modes are invisible to Tier-1/Tier-2.
#  * v1.16.1:main.go:236 STILL defaults --webhook-port to 9443. The flip to 0 exists only here.
#  * palette config/vendorcrd/vsphere/newns/kustomization.yaml passes only
#    `--leader-elect --namespace=$(NAMESPACE) --sync-period=2m` — NO --webhook-port — and
#    base/core-base.yaml has NO /tmp/k8s-webhook-server/serving-certs mount (that mount appears only
#    in global/core-global.yaml:7343). Lose the default flip and every per-tenant capv-controller-
#    manager starts a webhook server with no serving cert -> CrashLoopBackOff in every tenant ns.
#  * Lose the if/else GATING instead and the webhook pod (global overlay: --webhook-port=9443
#    --leader-elect=false) ALSO runs AddCluster/Machine/VM/DeploymentZone controllers alongside every
#    tenant controller, with leader election off -> duplicate reconciliation of the same VMs.
#  * Not a mechanical merge: main.go went 496 -> 752 lines, webhook types were renamed
#    (webhooks.VSphereClusterTemplateWebhook -> webhooks.VSphereClusterTemplate), setupClusterCache
#    gained (secretCachingClient, isSupervisorCRDLoaded), setupSupervisorControllers gained
#    secretCachingClient, and supervisor webhooks now take controllerCtx.NetworkProvider.
# Needs a human to read the resolved main.go and confirm BOTH the default and the gating.

column3: palette 2-pod model; target still defaults 9443 and newns passes no --webhook-port + no cert mount -> lose flip = tenant CrashLoop, lose gating = double reconcile; main.go 496->752 diverged

column1: # 3670335d "Fixed vsphere cluster upgrade stuck 1.22->1.23" — cannot be merged, only re-implemented,
# and the only coherent re-implementation changes semantics the fork never actually had.
#  * Real fork behavior IS absent from the target: v1.16.1:controllers/vspherevm_controller.go:239
#    returns errors.Wrapf unconditionally when the VSphereDeploymentZone Get fails.
#  * But the fork's own version is latently broken (round-1 finding, re-confirmed): its NotFound
#    branches only log and do NOT return, so control falls through to
#    Get(Name: vsphereDeploymentZone.Spec.FailureDomain) on a zero-valued struct — an EMPTY name —
#    which errors anyway. The fix as written likely never worked on that path.
#  * So "port the intent" means inventing new code. The only coherent port (tolerate NotFound and
#    proceed with vsphereFailureDomain == nil, which v1.16.1 already permits when no FD is set)
#    makes a nil failure domain reachable while an FD IS assigned -> vm.Spec.Datacenter/Datastore/
#    Folder/ResourcePool/Network overrides silently skipped -> VM placed on defaults instead of
#    erroring loudly. Silent wrong-placement is worse than the wedge it replaces.
#  * v1beta2 also changed Machine.Spec.FailureDomain *string -> string (target:234 `!= ""`), so the
#    fork's `*failureDomain` deref cannot apply as-is.
# Customer-facing bug fix (PCP-52) whose correct semantics are a product decision, not a merge.

column3: fork impl latently broken (NotFound falls through to empty-name Get); any real port makes nil failure-domain reachable -> silent VM misplacement instead of loud error; *string->string in v1beta2
